quickAnswer: Northborough is among the newer towns we serve: only 10.0% of its housing units predate 1940 (44th of 50), and the median home was built in 1980. Oil, at 41.4% of homes, narrowly leads gas at 39.3%, and National Grid is the electric utility.
body: ## One of the youngest housing stocks we work in

The 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) lists 5,934 housing units in Northborough. Only 595 of them, 10.0%, date from 1939 or earlier. That ranks 44th of the 50 towns we serve, and the middle town sits at 16.6%. The median Northborough home was built in 1980, five years later than the 1975 median of the middle town, and just 49.8% of units predate 1980, against 57.2% in the middle town.

One band towers over the rest: 1980 to 1999, at 1,961 units (33.0%). Another 1,020 (17.2%) went up in 2000 or later. With so few units from before 1940, boilers and furnaces of any age still need sizing against the house they serve. Newer construction is often tighter and can have a smaller heating load, but the only way to know is to measure it. Sizing comes from a measured heat loss for the specific house, and the age of a house is only a starting guess. A town with so many units in one band and the rest spread across other bands cannot be sized by a rule of thumb.
## Oil edges ahead of gas

Fuel oil heats 2,408 occupied homes (41.4%), and utility gas heats 2,282 (39.3%). The oil share is above the 36.5% of the middle town and the gas share is below its 41.9%. In the rankings, Northborough is 22nd of 50 for the highest share of oil heating and 27th for utility gas, so it sits near the middle on both. The ACS counts 15,647 residents, the 19th-largest population of the 50 towns. For an owner with a tired oil boiler, that near tie makes the next step an open comparison between another oil unit, gas if a main passes the house, and a heat pump.
## Owners, detached houses and few renters

Of 5,812 occupied homes, 84.7% are owner-occupied, so most repair and replacement decisions sit with the people living in the house. The 887 renter households (15.3%) are the smaller group, ranking 28th of 50, and the State Sanitary Code covers their heat as well. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $548,400, a little under the middle town's $579,150.
## A settlement older than its houses

Europeans set up a plantation here on May 14, 1656, and the district of Northborough was established within Westborough on January 23, 1766. It became a town on August 23, 1775, and on June 20, 1807 part of neighboring Marlborough was annexed. The town's first meeting house was established in 1746. Against that long history, only 10.0% of the units in the ACS date from 1939 or earlier, so the oldest houses are a minority.

The town covers 18.8 square miles, nearly all of it land, and U.S. Route 20, Route 9 and Route 135 are among the roads that link it to its neighbors. Marlborough lies due east, Westborough to the south, and Shrewsbury to the west, which is the town that separates Northborough from Worcester. The town sits about 302 feet above sea level on average.
## National Grid and the rebate terms

The town is on National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory list, which makes Mass Save the first program to check for a heat pump. Amounts, dates and the weatherization test are spelled out on our [heat pump page](/cities/northborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is Northborough's housing newer than most MetroWest towns?
faq.a: Yes, in the ACS 2022 figures. Northborough's median home was built in 1980 against 1975 for the middle town, and 10.0% of units date from 1939 or earlier, 44th of 50 towns. Newer housing can still be mis-sized, so the load gets measured house by house.

faq.q: Is it worth converting a Northborough oil boiler to gas?
faq.a: Only if gas is actually available at your street, and that is something to confirm early. Oil and gas are close in Northborough, at 41.4% and 39.3% of occupied homes, so both are common. A heat pump is the third option, and the estimate can price all three. Where the numbers favor a change, the load assessment shows the right size.

faq.q: Does National Grid offer heat pump rebates in Northborough?
faq.a: Northborough is in National Grid's territory, so Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate is the program to look at first. The house must meet its weatherization test, and amounts and dates can change, so confirm at masssave.com before ordering equipment.

faq.q: Are there many renters in Northborough?
faq.a: Fewer than in the middle town. The ACS 2022 counts 887 renter households, 15.3% of the total, against 16.4% for the middle town, and Northborough ranks 28th of 50 for renter share. The other 4,925 households (84.7%) own their homes.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 2,408 Northborough homes (41.4%) and gas heats 2,282 (39.3%), so a replacement is a live choice between fuels. The median home dates to 1980, newer than the housing in most towns we serve.
body: ## Oil and gas, nearly level

Northborough ranks 22nd of 50 towns for oil heat and 27th for utility gas, which puts it near the middle on both. The two fuels sit within a couple of points of each other. That makes the first question on a replacement job unusually open: stay with oil, move to gas where service reaches the house, or look at a heat pump.
## What the age bands say

The largest band is 1980 to 1999 at 1,961 units (33.0%). Next come 1,259 units from 1960 to 1979 and 1,099 from 1940 to 1959. Houses from different bands ask different things of a boiler or furnace, and the original piping or ducts may not suit a new unit's output or venting.
## The smaller fuel groups

Electricity heats 704 homes (12.1%), ranking 19th of 50. Bottled gas heats 269 (4.6%), wood heats 63, solar 16, and another 60 use other fuels or coal. Resistance electric heat is a natural candidate for the [heat pump route](/cities/northborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). A propane household can weigh its tank fuel against gas or electric.
## Gas equipment and the permit

A gas furnace or boiler swap is a permitted job: a licensed plumber or gas fitter files for it, and an inspection follows the installation. Your building department can tell you what a particular job requires, and ours will ask the right questions at the estimate.
## Rented homes

Northborough's 887 renter households fall under the State Sanitary Code: during the heating season, heat must hold at 68 F through the day and evening and 64 F overnight (105 CMR 410.201). The landlord carries the cost unless the lease assigns it elsewhere. This is general information, not legal advice.
## Calling us
Dial (508) 786-8755 at any hour for an emergency. The estimate is written, free, and in your hands before work begins. For the bigger picture, see the [Northborough page](/cities/northborough).

faq.q: How do I tell whether a Northborough furnace needs replacing?
faq.a: Age, repeat repairs and rising bills are common signs, and a cracked heat exchanger is a safety issue that usually ends the discussion. A technician can test the unit and say which case you are in. A written estimate comes before any work.

faq.q: Can I switch from oil to a heat pump?
faq.a: Often, but sizing decides how much of the house a heat pump can carry. Oil heats 2,408 Northborough homes, so the question comes up a lot. Some homes run a heat pump for everything, and others keep the old system as a backup.

faq.q: Is a houseful of electric baseboard a reason to look at a heat pump?
faq.a: It can be. The ACS 2022 counts 704 Northborough homes on electric heat, and resistance heat converts each unit of electricity to one unit of heat, which a heat pump can improve on. The load assessment shows how much of the house a heat pump could carry.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Northborough has 4,508 single-family detached houses (76.0%), 546 townhouses and 502 units in buildings of five or more. Each needs a different cooling plan, and many older homes were built without central air.
body: ## What kind of home are you cooling?

The ACS 2022 counts 4,508 detached houses in Northborough, 76.0% of all units, plus 546 attached townhouses (9.2%). Buildings of five or more units hold 502 units (8.5%). A detached house gives the most freedom: a condenser can go outside and either ducts or a ductless system can reach most rooms. For a townhouse or apartment, outdoor equipment may be limited, so ask the association or landlord first.
## Ducts or no ducts

Many older homes were built without central air, and a ducted retrofit can be hard to fit. Houses from 2000 or later, 1,020 units here, may be likelier to have ducts planned with cooling in mind, though each house differs.
- **Central air:** best where the ducts are sound and sized for the airflow.
- **Ductless mini-split:** useful for additions, upper floors and houses without ducts.
- **Heat pump:** heats and cools from one system, as described on the [heat pump page](/cities/northborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## A middle-aged housing stock

With a median build year of 1980, the typical Northborough house is neither the oldest in MetroWest nor among the newest. Another 1,961 units date from 1980 to 1999, the largest band in town. We look at what each house actually has instead of guessing from its decade.
## Sizing, not just brand

A unit that is too big cycles on and off without drying the air well. A unit that is too small runs constantly in a heat wave. Sizing should come from the house, including the insulation and the windows, not from the nameplate on the old unit.
## Multi-unit buildings

Northborough has 187 units in two-unit buildings and 191 in buildings of three or four units. In these, the outdoor placement, the electrical panel and the neighbors' windows all enter the decision, and it helps to settle them before equipment is ordered.
## When it stops cooling

If a system quits, check the thermostat, the breaker and the filter. After that, a technician can look at the coil, the refrigerant circuit and the outdoor unit. Call (508) 786-8755 for a free written estimate before repair work starts.

faq.q: Is central air or a mini-split better for my Northborough house?
faq.a: It depends on the ducts. If good ductwork already exists, central air is often simpler. If it does not, or the house has an addition or an upper floor that never cooled well, a mini-split can avoid new duct runs. We compare both at the estimate.

faq.q: Can I cool a Northborough townhouse with a ductless system?
faq.a: Often, because a ductless system needs only a thin line between the indoor and outdoor units, though the outdoor placement may be limited by the association. The ACS 2022 counts 546 attached townhouses in town. Ask your association first.

faq.q: Do houses built after 1980 cool more easily?
faq.a: Not as a rule. Northborough has 1,961 units from 1980 to 1999 and 1,020 from 2000 or later, and layout, ducts and window exposure vary within each group. A load check for your own house gives the answer.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Northborough is in National Grid territory, so Mass Save is the first rebate to check. Oil heats 2,408 homes here, more than any other fuel, and 2,953 units predate 1980, so weatherization status matters.
body: ## Utility and program

Northborough is on National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company list, so Mass Save is the program to check first. The 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500, and the house must be weatherized. Conditions and dates are on the [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Where a heat pump replaces a fuel

The ACS 2022 counts 2,408 oil homes (41.4%), 704 on electricity (12.1%) and 269 on bottled gas (4.6%). Those are the groups where a heat pump takes over from something burned or from resistance heat. Oil is the largest of the three by a wide margin, and a failing oil boiler is the natural moment to price a heat pump alongside another oil unit. Another 2,282 homes (39.3%) use gas, where the choice is usually to add a heat pump beside the existing equipment.
## Age against the weatherization test

Mass Save asks whether the house is already weatherized, and age is one shortcut. In Northborough, 1,020 units (17.2%) date from 2000 or later, including 494 from 2010 on. The 2,953 units built before 1980 (49.8%) are where a Home Energy Assessment is likeliest to matter, and the 1,961 units from 1980 to 1999 fall in between.
## House types

With 4,508 detached houses (76.0%), most Northborough heat pumps would be outdoor units beside a single house, often as multi-head ductless systems or a ducted set-up. The 502 units in buildings of five or more face building rules on outdoor equipment, and the 546 townhouses may too.
## Sizing before quoting

A heat pump sized too small can leave rooms cold in January, and one sized too large can cycle too often. We assess the heating load before quoting. In some houses a heat pump carries everything, and in others it works with the old system as backup. The cooling side is covered on the [air conditioning page](/cities/northborough/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: Is a heat pump realistic for an oil-heated Northborough home?
faq.a: Often. Oil is the leading fuel here at 41.4% of occupied homes, so many owners face the question. A heat pump can take over the whole load in a well-insulated house, or it can share the load with the old boiler. A measured heat loss decides which.

faq.q: Does my Northborough house need weatherizing first?
faq.a: For the Mass Save whole-home rebate, a house built before 2000 needs either an assessment that recommends under $1,000 of work or completed recommendations. Northborough has 2,953 units built before 1980, so for many an assessment is the first step.

faq.q: Will a heat pump keep my Northborough house warm in January?
faq.a: It can, if it is sized correctly and the house is reasonably tight. That is why we assess the heating load first. In some houses a heat pump carries the whole load, and in others it is paired with the existing system.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil heats 2,408 Northborough homes, more than any other fuel, and oil equipment needs cleaning every year. Owners hold 84.7% of households, so most service decisions rest with the person living in the house.
body: ## A routine for each fuel

Fuel oil leads here at 41.4% of occupied homes, and an oil boiler or furnace is due for cleaning every year. Gas, at 2,282 homes, brings a different list: burner, heat exchanger, venting and safety controls. Heat pumps, which are on the rise as an alternative, need clean filters and a clear outdoor unit.
## What a visit can cover
- Burner and combustion checks where fuel is burned.
- Filter, blower and coil inspection.
- Flue and venting inspection, a safety item.
- Thermostat and control checks.

Of the occupied homes, 187 sit in two-unit buildings and 191 in buildings of three or four units. Where one boiler serves several households, a failure reaches everyone at once, so servicing it before the heating season is a sensible habit. Wood heats 63 homes (1.1%), and a wood or oil chimney is another item for a yearly look.
## Houses with more than one household

In the ACS, 187 Northborough units sit in two-unit buildings and 191 in buildings of three or four units. Where one boiler serves several households, a failure reaches everyone at once, so servicing it before the heating season is a sensible habit. Wood heats 63 homes (1.1%), and a chimney or flue serving a wood or oil appliance generally needs an inspection each year too.
## Owners hold most of the keys

With 4,925 owner-occupied households (84.7%), most Northborough maintenance is booked by the person who lives with the equipment. The 887 renter households (15.3%) depend on the landlord to schedule it.
## The calendar
Heating season starts around mid-September, so late summer is the time for heating service, and spring suits cooling service. Call (508) 786-8755 and describe what you have.
## Newer equipment still needs attention

The median home here was built in 1980, and 1,961 units come from 1980 to 1999. Equipment in houses of that era has been running a long time, and the first sign of trouble is often a noise, a smell or a slow start. A visit can turn up a worn part, a leaking boiler or a cracked heat exchanger, and the estimate for what to do is written and free.

faq.q: How often should I have my oil boiler cleaned?
faq.a: Yearly, ahead of mid-September when heating season begins. A cleaning can also reveal worn parts you can plan to replace on your own schedule rather than in an emergency.

faq.q: Do heat pumps need maintenance too?
faq.a: Yes, though the routine is lighter. Filters need regular cleaning, outdoor units need to stay clear of leaves and snow, and a technician should look at the system periodically. Skipping this can reduce performance over time.

faq.q: Do newer Northborough houses still need a yearly visit?
faq.a: Generally yes. With 1,020 units built in 2000 or later, many local systems are comparatively young, but filters, drains and controls still collect dust and wear. A yearly look finds small problems early.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: About a third of Northborough homes (33.0%) were built from 1980 to 1999, and tighter construction can hold moisture and fumes unless ventilation works. The town's 10.0% from 1939 or earlier leak differently.
body: ## The 1980 to 1999 band leads

Northborough's biggest group is the 1,961 units built from 1980 to 1999, and 1,020 more date from 2000 or later. Homes from those decades are usually tighter than much older ones, which makes filters, humidity and ventilation the main levers for indoor air. Older houses leak more, which dilutes some pollutants but can also bring in dust, pollen and basement air.
## Older stock in a younger town

Only 595 units date from 1939 or earlier, 10.0% of the total. Houses that old are the minority here, and a plaster-and-wood interior can respond to dry winters and damp summers in ways a newer house does not. With 122 vacant units in the ACS count (2.1%), Northborough has few empty houses, so most of its air is lived-in air with cooking and showers adding to it.
## Moisture and humidity

Winter heat dries indoor air, and humid summers bring the moisture back. In a tight house, cooking and showers can add moisture that lingers without working exhaust fans. Musty smells and mold tend to follow damp basements and weak exhaust, so those are worth checking first.
## The practical list
- **Filters:** a clean filter of the right grade reduces dust moving through a ducted system.
- **Ventilation:** kitchen and bathroom fans should vent outside, and very tight houses may benefit from a planned fresh-air source.
- **Ductwork:** leaks can pull air from attics, basements and garages.
- **Duct cleaning:** useful after renovation or visible contamination, not always needed.
## Fuel-burning equipment
Oil heats 2,408 Northborough homes and gas heats 2,282. A carbon monoxide alarm and a clear flue matter in every one of them, and an annual combustion check is how a failing vent gets noticed.
## Newest houses
Only 8.3% of Northborough units, 494, went up in 2010 or later. Houses that new are often built tight, so mechanical ventilation can matter more for them.
## Working with the HVAC system

Air quality equipment such as filters, humidifiers and ventilators works through the heating and cooling system, so a wrongly sized system can undercut it. To talk through your house, call (508) 786-8755. The [heat pump page](/cities/northborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers equipment options.

faq.q: Does a tighter house need a ventilator?
faq.a: It can help. A tight house keeps in moisture, cooking fumes and furnishing chemicals unless ventilation carries them out. Start by checking that bathroom and kitchen fans work and vent outdoors. A ventilator is the next step if problems persist.
Not by default. Cleaning is sometimes worthwhile after a renovation or if ducts are visibly dirty or contaminated. In other cases filter changes and an inspection are enough.

faq.q: Are older Northborough houses worse for air quality?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Older houses leak more air, which dilutes some pollutants but admits dust, pollen and damp air. Only 10.0% of units here date from 1939 or earlier, and a visit can show whether moisture or ducts are the issue.
